Appearance:
Shri Manoj Malviya - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate for the respondent

Order 
This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant(s) assailing the impugned award dated 14.03.2019 passed by Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Neemuch (M.P.) in Claim Case No.198/2018, whereby an amount of Rs.4,90,600/-
along with interest has been awarded to the survivors of the deceased Shivcharan @ Kalu, who passed away in road traffic accident which occurred on 03.05.2017 involving the offending vehicle Tractor No. MP 44 M 2188.
2.

Learned counsel for the appellant(s) submits that the income of the deceased has been assessed as Rs.4500/- which is on the lower side, whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.7125/-.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
He further submits that in the head of consortium only Rs.40,000/-
has been awarded by the learned Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8921 2 MA-2752-2019 Tribunal whereas both the dependents are entitled for consortium amount @
Rs.40,000/- each.

Learned counsel further submits that no amount has been awarded in the head of loss of estate, however Rs.15,000/- should have been awarded as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680 (para 59.8).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680 (para 59.8)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Looking to the age of the deceased 48 years on the date of the incident, 10% future prospects should have been awarded.
On these submissions, he prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.

3 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that learned Claims Tribunal has taken due care of all the parameters for assessing just and proper compensation, therefore, no interference is required by allowing this appeal, hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.

4. Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5. In light of the aforesaid, where the income of the deceased is taken on guess work, Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.

Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on 03.05.2017 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.7125/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour'
and for this judgment passed by the Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. vs.
Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198 shall be referred.

entities.text:
Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. vs.
Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the head of future prospects, 10% is to be added as per directions given in para 59.3 & 59.4 of the judgment passed in the case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8921 3 MA-2752-2019 o f Pranay Sethi (supra) and multiplier of 11
has already been properly applied.
In the head loss of estate Rs.15,000/- is added.

In the head of consortium, both the claimants are entitled for consortium amount @ Rs.40,000/- each as per judgment passed in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram @
Chuhru Ram (2018) 18 SCC 130 which has been approved in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Others (2021) 11 SCC 780 .
Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
Loss of Rs.7125/- + Rs.712/- (10% FP) = Rs.7837 x 12 = Dependency: Rs.94,044/- -
1/3 (PE) x 11 Multiplier = Rs.6,89,656/-

6 . Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.7,99,656/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.4,90,600/-
.
Accordingly, the appellant(s) are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.3,09,056/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7 . The appeal is valued as Rs.3 Lakhs and for the rest of the amount, the claimant(s) will pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8921 4 MA-2752-2019 from today and only thereafter enhanced amount will be disbursed.

In case the appellant(s) fails to pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days then beyond 30 days Meera Bai vs Nareshchandra Chouhan on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168733043/
2 interest will not be payable till filing of the Court fees.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate, which was fixed in the impugned award and the other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
8 . Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off in above terms.
